title: Week 19 Check-In · The Whipping Boy
description: This week the story turned upside down. The outlaws mixed up the two boys, decided Jemmy was the prince, and Jemmy wrote a ransom note to the king. You practiced compound sentences, the root port (carry), and consonant-le syllables. Show what you know!

questions.text: Which is a correctly punctuated compound sentence?
options: Jemmy wanted to escape, but the prince refused to move.
Jemmy wanted to escape but, the prince refused to move.
Jemmy wanted to escape but the prince refused to move.
questions.from: 19.3 Grammar (where the comma goes), 19.4 mistake hunt

questions.text: Join these into a compound sentence: “The outlaws captured them. Jemmy knew they were in serious trouble.”
Write your own compound sentence about two characters making different choices.
The root port means “carry.” Break apart the word export. What does it mean?
questions.status: new (old Q4 tested the suffix -er, not taught)

questions.text: The root port means “carry.” Something that is portable —
options: can be carried from place to place

questions.text: Choose one: transport, import, or report. Write a sentence that shows what the word means.
Each word ends in a consonant-le syllable. Write each word and split it into syllables with a slash mark (example: ta/ble). little · candle · purple
questions.status: new (old Q7 tested open syllables, not taught)

questions.text: Explain the consonant-le rule in your own words. Give one example word.
Which word is split into syllables the right way?
What do the outlaws plan to do with the boy they think is the prince? Use a detail from the passage.
The passage says being royal “didn’t seem to be any advantage at all.” What does this mean? Why is it surprising, given how the story started?
Do you think Jemmy or the prince is better prepared for this situation? Use details to explain your thinking.

Model sentence: “The prince could have gone home, but he stayed — and Jemmy was struck dumb.” Notice the contrast (could have / but), the dash, and the short ending. Write your own sentence about a character’s choice using this pattern.
questions.status: fixed (old model said Jemmy stayed instead of running; that is not what happens)

questions.text: The prince is used to giving orders, but now he has no power. Write 1–2 sentences predicting how this situation might change him.

passage.title: Reading passage (summary of Ch. 7–8)
passage.text: Hold-Your-Nose Billy watched the two boys closely. The ragged whipping boy knew his letters, but the boy who called himself a prince could not even sign his own name. “Something’s amiss here,” Billy said. He decided Jemmy must be the real prince and made plans to trade him to the king for a ransom of gold. The real prince shouted that he was His Royal Highness, but Billy told him to hush. For the first time, being royal didn’t seem to be any advantage at all.
